geo.label: March lift-off priced; curve bear-flattening
parts: Macro Stance

The US starts February with growth decelerating from a strong base and a Federal Reserve committed to tightening into it. Reuters reported the Fed is likely to hike in March as Powell vowed a sustained inflation fight [[n1241]], and a Reuters poll of economists expects three hikes this year to tame unruly inflation [[n1908]]. The data argue for patience on growth but not on inflation: the January ISM manufacturing index eased to 57.6 from 58.7 [[n1989]] [[n1872]], still firmly expansionary, while CNBC counted 4.6 million more job openings than unemployed workers in December [[n1996]]. Fiscal support is fading as well, with Senator Joe Manchin declaring Build Back Better 'dead' [[n2052]]. Our stance is Mixed: earnings momentum is genuine, but the policy path caps how much investors will pay for it.
Rates & Curve

The Treasury curve is doing the classic pre-hike move. The 2-year yield closed at 1.18% and the 10-year at 1.81%, a 10Y-2Y spread of +63 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-01). Over 20 observations the 2-year rose 40 bps from 0.78% and the 10-year 18 bps from 1.63%, compressing the spread by 22 bps: a bear flattening, with the curve still moderately steep. In the latest five observations the 2-year added 16 bps against 3 bps for the 10-year, so the front end is still carrying the repricing. Standard Chartered expects the curve to flatten and possibly invert this year [[n2045]]. Equities have stopped fighting it: the S&P 500 closed at 4,546.54 points, +0.69% on the day and +4.36% over five sessions, VIX fell 11.56% to 21.96 points and DXY eased 0.16% to 96.39 points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).
New / Most Important

The decisive news came after the bell. Reuters reported that Google propelled record Alphabet revenue, driving the shares up 8% [[n0095]], with a 20-for-1 stock split on top [[n0806]]; AMD rose 10% after issuing a strong 2022 sales outlook [[n0744]], while Electronic Arts' revenue forecast missed estimates after the Battlefield flop [[n0781]]. The message is that investors will still pay for visible forward growth in a rising-rate tape, while a soft forecast leaves nowhere to hide. The macro backdrop is less forgiving: CNBC warns that after a huge year for growth the economy is about to 'slam into a wall' [[n1985]], and the Nasdaq only narrowly missed its worst January ever [[n0092]].
Playbook ✓

Action: stay long quality mega-cap growth that has just reset expectations higher (Alphabet's record quarter, AMD's 2022 outlook), funded from long-duration Treasuries and unprofitable growth, and keep 2s10s flatteners on. Trigger: the 2-year holding at or above 1.18% while the S&P 500 holds its 4,546.54-point close (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-01; Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01) would confirm that equities can absorb a March lift-off. What changes the call: a VIX reversal that erases the 11.56% one-day drop, or a growth scare that drags the 2-year back toward 0.78%, would favour duration over equities and end the flattener.

geo.label: ECB on hold; gas premium easing
parts: Macro Stance

Europe's macro story is an energy-price shock that may be peaking while the geopolitical risk behind it is not. Dutch TTF gas fell 10.04% to 76.17 EUR/MWh and is down 18.61% over five sessions, and the STOXX 600 rose 1.28% to 474.86 points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), as Reuters reported the Yamal pipeline set to resume westbound flows to Germany [[n0837]]. Our stance is Mixed: cheaper gas relieves margins and household budgets, but the supply route remains hostage to Moscow, and the DAX at 15,619.39 points is still 3.30% below its level of early January.
Activity & Inflation

Price pressure is broad but uneven. German inflation dropped in January [[n1213]], and BNP Paribas flags an unusual gap between French and German inflation [[n1227]]. Deutsche Bank asks whether higher energy prices are here to stay [[n1226]], and Bruegel examines who is suffering most from rising inflation [[n1236]]. The ECB remains the outlier among major central banks: a Reuters poll sees euro zone inflation burning hotter while ECB rates stay on ice [[n1145]], even as OMFIF argues the bank must tighten now to avoid a sharper correction later [[n1223]]. That gap between a hawkish Fed and a patient ECB keeps European financial conditions loose relative to the US.
New / Most Important

Supply security is the swing factor. Qatar is seeking EU guarantees that emergency gas stays within the bloc [[n1199]], and Reuters' explainer asks how far Qatari cargoes can offset Russian disruption [[n1202]]. Politics is a smaller drag: The Conversation argues Mattarella's reappointment as Italy's president is a huge relief for the West [[n1233]].
Playbook ✓

Action: overweight euro-area cyclicals and banks through FEZ, which closed at 45.86 USD (+1.17%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), and hold a small TTF upside hedge. Trigger: TTF staying below its 80.43 EUR/MWh close of January 3 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-03) while Yamal flows resume. What changes the call: a renewed gas spike on Ukraine headlines, or an ECB that holds rates while inflation keeps surprising, would compress real incomes and flip the cyclical overweight.

geo.label: PBOC easing through a holiday-thin market
parts: Macro Stance

China is closed for the Lunar New Year, so investors are working from a pre-holiday data set and a policy bias that is turning steadily more supportive. The economy finished 2021 strong on paper, with Global Times reporting GDP growth of 8.1%, the fastest in a decade [[n0107]], but momentum entering 2022 is weak. The People's Bank of China has already moved: the BBC reported rate cuts as growth slows [[n0106]], and CNBC noted a cut to key lending rates, one of them the first in nearly two years [[n0113]]. Bloomberg's framing is the right one: as the Fed hikes, China's central bank is seizing the moment for stimulus [[n0120]]. Our stance is Mixed: policy is easing, but property and COVID controls still set the growth path.
PMIs & Activity

January surveys confirmed a soft start. Reuters reported that official factory activity growth slowed as demand waned with COVID surging [[n0170]], while the Caixin gauge showed outright contraction as lockdowns bit [[n0166]]. ABN AMRO concludes the January PMIs indicate quarter-on-quarter growth will drop in the first quarter [[n0179]], echoing an official who warned in January that factories face 'rather large' downward pressure in the first quarter [[n0116]]. Some 2021 data were firmer: industrial profits rebounded as production improved [[n0155]], and fixed-asset investment rose 4.9% [[n0109]]. The mismatch matters: backward-looking strength gives Beijing room to be patient, while the forward indicators argue for more easing before activity can stabilise.
Credit Impulse

Until the next lending data, the credit impulse has to be read through policy. The January moves, cuts to medium-term lending and reverse-repo rates reported by Fibre2Fashion [[n0117]] on top of the lending-rate cut, lower the marginal cost of credit, but transmission depends on banks' willingness to lend into property. Nikkei Asia's report that major Evergrande creditor Minsheng faces a wave of bad loans [[n0125]] shows the problem: lenders carrying developer losses ration risk even as funding costs fall. The likely sequence is a turn in the impulse from a low base, led by policy-directed lending rather than households, which helps materials and infrastructure before it helps consumption.
Property

Property remains the binding constraint. AFR reported that Beijing is considering breaking up Evergrande to contain the crisis [[n0136]], and Oaktree Capital has seized a second Evergrande property in China [[n0204]], a sign that creditors are enforcing on collateral. Reuters' insight on the developer's showpiece resort island [[n0188]] captures the stranded-asset problem, while Bloomberg found cities selling land to themselves as the property crisis leaves cities selling land to themselves [[n0126]]. The one stabilising sign is pricing: new home prices fell less in December on promotions and easing curbs [[n0104]]. Until sales volumes respond to lower rates, local-government finances remain the channel through which property drags on growth.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Infrastructure ambition is back on the table, with the South China Morning Post listing six controversial mega-projects under discussion [[n0169]], but external friction is building again. A U.S. trade official said China failed to meet its 'Phase 1' commitments [[n0208]], and CNN explains why Biden is keeping Trump's China tariffs in place [[n0131]]. The WTO has ruled that China can impose 645 million dollars of retaliatory tariffs on U.S. imports [[n0121]], and the EU has escalated its trade dispute with Beijing over Lithuania [[n0146]]. CNBC adds that a crackdown on Chinese IPOs in the U.S. could make investors think twice about betting on Chinese tech [[n0124]]. Policy therefore pulls two ways: domestic easing supports the cycle, while external pressure caps the multiple investors will pay for it.
Markets & Flows

Mainland and Hong Kong markets are shut, so the last prints are stale: the Shanghai Composite closed at 3,361.44 points, down 4.57% over five sessions and 7.12% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-28), while the Hang Seng finished at 23,802.26 points, up 2.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). The South China Morning Post noted the Hang Seng logged a January gain but closed the Year of the Ox with a slump [[n0186]]. U.S.-listed proxies kept trading: KWEB rose 0.67% to 37.66 USD and FXI 0.66% to 38.19 USD, while the A-share tracker ASHR is down 6.48% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Offshore internet up, onshore A-shares down: investors are rewarding the policy pivot in platform names while onshore pricing still reflects growth risk.
New / Most Important

The new element is the overlap of the Winter Olympics, COVID controls and the post-holiday restart. Axios argues COVID threatens China's Olympic prestige [[n0197]], and Hong Kong is locking down homes in a lesson taken from Beijing [[n0162]]. Supply chains are the transmission channel: HSBC warns that disruptions in China can create ripple effects across the global supply chain [[n0184]]. Iron ore is the early tell, with Singapore futures falling more than 6% [[n0064]] before mainland traders return.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay overweight offshore China internet through KWEB and the Alibaba ADR (BABA), which closed at 127.22 USD and is up 6.78% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), and stay underweight onshore A-shares via ASHR until property sales stabilise. Trigger: a further PBOC rate or reserve-requirement cut after the holiday, with the Hang Seng holding above its 23,274.75-point level of early January. What changes the call: a post-holiday COVID wave that forces factory closures, or a fresh U.S. delisting push, would hit the offshore leg hardest. ⚠ Divergence: policy is easing and offshore internet is rallying, yet the PMIs, the Caixin contraction and iron ore's slide say real activity is still losing momentum.

geo.label: BOJ anchored; output wobbling
parts: Macro Stance

Japan is the major economy least exposed to the global tightening wave, which is both its support and its problem. The Nikkei 225 closed at 27,078.48 points, +0.28% on the day but -5.95% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), lagging the U.S. rebound. Reuters reported that the BOJ is debating how to message an eventual rate hike as inflation perks up [[n1403]], yet nothing in the data forces a move: factory output dipped more than expected as risks emerged [[n1423]]. Security risk is rising too, after North Korea claimed a test of a missile capable of striking U.S. bases in Guam and Japan [[n1360]]. Our stance is Mixed: valuations are undemanding, but a domestic catalyst is missing.
Activity & Currency

Activity is uneven. The Japan Times says the job market showed signs of healing before Omicron spread [[n1435]], and Nippon.com reports 2021 imports and exports near record highs [[n1433]]. Inflation is arriving through goods prices: the 'miracle' Umaibo snack is getting its first price hike after decades [[n1408]], and the Asahi Shimbun warns surging prices will pinch consumers and derail recovery hopes [[n1419]]. On the currency, the dollar's biggest weekly rise in seven months on rate bets [[n1413]] widens the policy gap with a BOJ that is still only debating its messaging, a tailwind for exporters. Toyota, which Reuters says remains the world's biggest car seller and widened its lead on Volkswagen [[n0542]], is up 5.77% over 20 sessions at 2,227.00 JPY, while Tokyo Electron is down 16.46% at 55,370.00 JPY (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer exporters and autos such as Toyota over domestic-demand names, and keep chip-equipment makers as a recovery option rather than a core long. Trigger: Advantest extending its 3.17% five-session rebound to 9,750.00 JPY (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01) alongside a firmer SOXX. What changes the call: a BOJ that pulls forward its hike messaging would remove the policy-gap tailwind for exporters, and a deeper output slump would hit autos first.

geo.label: Inflation shock; cash-rate debate
parts: Macro Stance

Australia's policy debate is now about when the cash rate rises, not whether it will. Governor Philip Lowe's February policy statement [[n0065]] follows what the AFR called a shock inflation spike to 3.5 per cent [[n0012]] and a jobless rate at a 13-year low [[n0007]]. Economists now predict rate increases from mid-2022 [[n0014]], and Future Fund chair Peter Costello says the RBA's credibility has been damaged [[n0059]]. Our stance is Mixed: the economy can absorb higher rates, but household leverage makes the transition fragile.
Demand & Financing

Housing is the transmission channel. Domain reports the median house price hit a record $1.066 million [[n0015]], so mortgage-rate sensitivity is high, and Bloomberg describes a bond meltdown haunting the central bank as inflation builds [[n0008]]. Markets are pricing caution rather than panic: the S&P/ASX 200 closed at 7,006.00 points, +0.49% on the day but -5.89% over 20 sessions, with Commonwealth Bank down 7.00% and CSL down 10.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Miners are the offset: BHP is up 8.27% over 20 sessions despite a 3.06% drop on the day, as Singapore iron ore futures fell more than 6% [[n0064]]. Corporate activity is a second support, with the AFR describing an M&A boom reshaping the ASX one deal at a time [[n0017]].
Playbook ✓

Action: favour miners over banks and long-duration growth, but size the miner exposure for an iron ore correction. Trigger: BHP holding above its 36.95 AUD close of December 31 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2021-12-31). What changes the call: guidance from the RBA pointing to a first hike earlier than mid-2022 would hit banks and housing-linked names, while a post-holiday rebound in Chinese steel demand would extend the miner leg.

geo.label: Rate hikes meet the anti-inflation shield
parts: Macro Stance

Poland combines the region's strongest growth with one of its sharpest inflation problems. GUS data show GDP grew 5.7% in 2021 [[n1596]], a strong rebound in Bankier's words [[n1605]], and Eurostat ranks Poland second-lowest for unemployment in the EU, 300Gospodarka reports [[n1652]]. But CPI ended 2021 at 8.6% [[n1470]], the highest in 21 years [[n1469]], and Credit Agricole has lifted its inflation forecast to 7.5% for 2022 and 5.5% for the following year [[n1473]]. Obserwator Gospodarczy still expects industry to be the economy's driving force in 2022 [[n1653]]. Rzeczpospolita warns that a slowdown is being masked by statistics, with inflation and rates already curbing appetites [[n1622]]. Our stance is Mixed: growth supports earnings, but inflation, a weak zloty and war risk on the eastern border keep the risk premium high.
Markets

Polish equities trade at a discount that already reflects much of the bad news. Strefa Inwestorów notes that Warsaw investors fear a crash and a crisis, which is why the market is valued really low [[n1599]], and Parkiet reported a rebound after the declines [[n1611]]. The Beta ETF WIG20TR closed at 38.26 PLN, +0.51% on the day and -2.95% over 20 sessions, while EPOL rose 1.36% to 20.81 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Banks lead: mBank jumped 5.29% to 489.80 PLN and is up 11.57% over five sessions, Bank Pekao is up 9.87% over 20 sessions at 136.95 PLN and PKO BP 5.15% at 48.00 PLN, as Strefa Inwestorów reports WIBOR still rising and banks certain of further rate hikes [[n1665]]. Outside finance the tape is mixed: Allegro rose 3.28% to 38.83 PLN, while the retail broker XTB fell 2.78% to 16.11 PLN. The currency is the weak link: FXMAG calls the zloty once again the worst-performing currency [[n1644]], which imports inflation and complicates the central bank's job.
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal policy has become an inflation tool. The government's Anti-Inflation Shield 2.0 started on February 1, Gov.pl announced [[n1657]], with lower VAT on food, energy and fuel [[n1610]]. Money.pl checked how far food prices actually fell after the VAT cut [[n1666]], and Interia asked whether the promised lower fuel prices reached the pumps [[n1647]]; Orlen chief Daniel Obajtek argues Poland now has the lowest fuel prices in Europe [[n1633]]. The trade-off is that the shield lowers headline CPI mechanically while supporting demand, and Credit Agricole has warned the food VAT cut will add to inflation [[n1466]]. Polski Ład adds noise: Rzeczpospolita tallies who gains or loses in take-home pay [[n1582]]. Governance risk sits on top, as Rzeczpospolita reports Glapiński's candidacy for a second NBP term is poorly rated [[n1602]] and the Sejm is delaying the election of Monetary Policy Council members [[n1523]].
Corporate & Sectors

Corporate news splits along energy and rates lines. Comparic noted Orlen shares at a one-month low despite record crude prices [[n1509]], and Subiektywnie o finansach issues a big warning against the Orlen–Lotos merger [[n1663]]; Orlen closed at 71.72 PLN, -4.58% over 20 sessions. Gas pricing is a live dispute, with wnp.pl reporting that Gazprom wants PGNiG to pay a surcharge [[n1485]]. Coal is the winner: JSW rose 6.30% to 42.04 PLN and is up 18.76% over 20 sessions after Bankier flagged its accelerating rebound [[n1478]]. KGHM gained 2.29% to 142.75 PLN, though its workforce is getting a bonus plus a 10% pay rise [[n1536]]. CD Projekt, at 180.94 PLN, benefits from gaming M&A, as Investing.com Polska tied its rise to Sony's Bungie deal [[n1659]]. Consumer names lag: Dino fell 8.63% over five sessions to 312.50 PLN, and Pepco is back at its IPO price [[n1515]] (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Utilities are the laggards: PGE, which has just published locations for new wind farms [[n1612]], is down 7.51% over 20 sessions at 7.56 PLN, a reminder that the energy transition needs capital just as funding costs rise.
Geopolitics & Security

Poland is on the front line of the Russia–Ukraine standoff, and the security response is accelerating. Reuters reports Britain, Poland and Ukraine are in cooperation talks over the Russian threat [[n1455]], which TVN24, citing the BBC, describes as a new alliance linking London, Kyiv and Warsaw [[n1585]]. TWZ reports Poland will send shoulder-fired anti-aircraft missiles to Ukraine [[n1457]]. Moscow's rhetoric is hardening: at a press conference with Viktor Orbán, Putin called NATO's enlargement to include Poland a fraud, Interia reported [[n1627]], and TVN24 has reported Russian airborne troops in Brest near the Polish border [[n1501]]. Warsaw has contingency plans to evacuate diplomats from Ukraine [[n1543]]. Energy is the economic channel: in a 300Gospodarka interview, Andrzej Sikora argues Poland will cope without Russian gas, but it will not be cheaper [[n1661]].
New / Most Important

The most important new fact is that the shield is now live: Biznes Wprost notes that lower VAT on fuel and food is not the only change taking effect [[n1664]]. Measured CPI will fall for tax reasons, which markets could misread as genuine disinflation. Business Insider Polska argues that a real reduction in inflation is all in Glapiński's hands [[n1640]], and Coface's chief expects a rise in insolvent companies [[n1655]]. For investors that means bank earnings upgrades now and credit costs later.
Playbook ✓

Action: hold Polish banks (PKO BP, Pekao, mBank) as the cleanest expression of rising WIBOR, keep the position smaller than the rate case alone would justify, and avoid domestic consumer names until real wages recover. Trigger: mBank holding above 455.00 PLN, its close of January 3 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-03), while WIBOR keeps rising. What changes the call: a military escalation on the Ukrainian border, or an NBP leadership outcome that weakens the zloty further, would turn banks from rate winners into risk-premium losers, and a sharp tax-driven fall in CPI could cap rate expectations. ⚠ Divergence: strong growth and rising bank stocks point to resilience, yet the zloty's weakness, record inflation and Russian troops near the border argue the risk premium should be rising, not falling.
Narrative

Technology is rebounding, but Barron's says January was historically bad for tech even after a two-day rally [[n1100]]. XLK closed at 162.39 USD, +7.16% over five sessions but -7.48% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), and the rebound is being led by earnings rather than by any relief in yields.
Reported

Apple's sales and profit topped estimates as the hit from chip shortages eased [[n0333]], producing its biggest one-day gain since July 2020 [[n0464]], and Microsoft beat on earnings and revenue with an upbeat fiscal third-quarter forecast [[n0988]]. The counterweight is Intel, whose first-quarter forecast missed the Street [[n1042]].
EPS Upside Watch

Software is where estimates can rise fastest: ServiceNow gained 18.47% and CrowdStrike 14.86% over five sessions, while Apple at 174.61 USD and Microsoft at 308.76 USD are still below their early-January levels (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Cash-rich platforms with raised guidance have the cleanest path to upgrades.
⚡ Breaking Convention

In a bear-flattening curve, net-cash mega-cap tech behaves more like a quality defensive than a duration asset. The pain is concentrated in unprofitable growth, which is why we stay Mixed on the sector but selectively long its leaders.
Narrative

Communication services carries the day's best fundamental news. XLC closed at 74.59 USD, +4.67% over five sessions and -4.64% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), and Alphabet's after-hours jump resets the sector's earnings anchor.
Reported

Deadline reports YouTube fourth-quarter ad sales jumped to $8.6B and Google Search hit $43B [[n0870]], and The Verge notes Alphabet broke $200 billion of annual revenue for the first time [[n1119]]. On the other side, AT&T will spin off WarnerMedia in its $43 billion Discovery merger and cut its dividend [[n0749]], and Electronic Arts' revenue forecast missed after the Battlefield flop [[n0781]].
EPS Upside Watch

Meta Platforms (FB), at 319.00 USD and up 6.28% over five sessions, is the obvious read-across from Google's ad strength. Netflix's 24.76% five-session rebound to 457.13 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01) followed Barron's report that Pershing Square bought $1 billion in shares [[n0395]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The sector's biggest risk is content liability rather than ads: TheWrap says Spotify lost $2 billion in value after Neil Young's protest over Joe Rogan [[n0587]], which shows how a platform controversy can move a multiple faster than subscriber numbers.
Narrative

Financials are the cleanest beneficiary of the bear flattening, because a 2-year yield up 40 bps over 20 observations lifts asset yields faster than deposit costs (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-01). XLF rose 1.38% to 39.60 USD, and Wells Fargo is up 9.60% over 20 sessions at 55.60 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).
Reported

Blackstone reported record fourth-quarter earnings [[n0339]], Nasdaq's profit topped Street views on an IPO surge and demand for investment products [[n1005]], and Visa said crypto-linked card usage hit $2.5 billion in its first quarter [[n0553]].
EPS Upside Watch

Net interest income upgrades should follow the front-end move: Bank of America at 46.94 USD and JPMorgan at 151.15 USD are the large-cap expressions, and Citigroup at 66.56 USD is already up 5.48% over 20 sessions. Card networks add volume leverage, with Visa up 15.03% and Mastercard 15.73% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01) after what Payments Industry Intelligence called monster revenue updates [[n0554]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The contrarian risk sits in payments rather than banks. PayPal's plunge on weak guidance [[n0831]] shows that fintech is being repriced as consumer-discretionary exposure, even as Wolfe Research's Darrin Peller argues its growth will be consistent [[n0866]].
Narrative

Energy remains the leadership trade. XLE rose 3.56% to 68.27 USD and is up 19.31% over 20 sessions, while Brent closed at 89.16 USD/bbl, +12.89% over 20 sessions despite a 2.25% dip on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Reuters said oil posted its biggest monthly gain in a year on tight supply and political tensions [[n1809]].
Reported

Exxon posted its biggest profit in seven years [[n0788]], with The New York Times putting fourth-quarter profit at $8.9 billion [[n0786]]. Chevron, by contrast, kicked off the industry's results with a miss [[n0478]].
EPS Upside Watch

Cash return is the EPS lever: ExxonMobil earned $23 billion in 2021 and initiated a $10 billion repurchase programme [[n1268]], and World Oil reports Exxon joining Chevron in the Permian surge as peers preach caution [[n1116]]. Schlumberger, up 24.59% over 20 sessions at 39.52 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), is the services lever on that activity, while OPEC barely increased output last month [[n1844]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The bear case is diplomatic, not demand-driven: The New York Times reports the U.S. and allies are close to reviving the nuclear deal with Iran [[n1367]], which would add barrels and could deflate the risk premium quickly.
Narrative

Industrials are split between freight winners and margin losers. XLI rose 1.38% to 102.13 USD but is down 2.68% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), consistent with a January ISM reading of 57.6 that still signals expansion at a slowing pace [[n1989]].
Reported

UPS offered a brighter view after an 'outstanding' 2021 and its shares hit a record high [[n0858]]. Caterpillar's sales soared but it warned of margin pressure [[n0476]], and FedEx suspended domestic express freight services on the Omicron hit [[n0794]]. Union Pacific is buying ten more all-electric locomotives from Caterpillar's Progress Rail [[n0731]], a small sign of rail capex.
EPS Upside Watch

Boeing is the upgrade candidate: CNBC reports it won a Qatar Airways order for 737 Max planes and new 777X freighters [[n0653]], and the stock rose 4.05% to 208.34 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Parcel pricing power is the other lever, with Supply Chain Dive expecting shipping to be even more expensive in 2022 [[n1105]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Boeing itself says Ukraine tensions are creating an 'adverse climate' for business [[n0652]], so the sector's geopolitical hedge is defence rather than civil aerospace: Lockheed Martin is up 9.21% over 20 sessions at 387.01 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).
Narrative

Consumer discretionary is the weakest large sector, with XLY at 186.07 USD, -11.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Real incomes are the problem: the Peterson Institute notes US wages are rising rapidly, but not enough to keep up with inflation [[n2037]].
Reported

Starbucks' sales rose as cost pressures increased [[n0842]], and McDonald's profit was hit by rising costs and pandemic curbs [[n0386]]. GM is the exception, forecasting earnings at or near record levels in 2022 as the chip shortage eases [[n0800]].
EPS Upside Watch

Amazon is the swing factor: GeekWire's preview has analysts expecting record revenue of $137B but lower profits [[n0752]], and the stock closed at 3,023.87 USD, -11.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). A margin beat there would do more for the index than any restaurant print, and Home Depot's plan to hire more than 100,000 associates [[n1132]] signals retailers still expect spring demand.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Tesla's recall of nearly 54,000 vehicles that may disobey stop signs [[n1856]] matters less than its index weight: at 931.25 USD and -22.38% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), Tesla is dragging the sector more than consumers are.
Narrative

Staples are a pricing-power test. XLP closed at 75.90 USD, -0.09% on the day and -1.56% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01): defensive, but lagging as the market rotates back into growth.
Reported

Diageo's sales jumped on premium spirits and bar restocking [[n0357]], Kraft Heinz is raising prices on Oscar Mayer hot dogs and Velveeta [[n1946]], and LVMH's Bernard Arnault says the group has pricing power to counter inflation but must be reasonable [[n0380]].
EPS Upside Watch

PepsiCo, at 172.34 USD, is extending its range with a hemp seed-infused drink under Rockstar Energy [[n0832]], and Costco closed at 508.41 USD, up 6.51% over five sessions. Price-led revenue growth should keep estimates intact even as volumes soften; Walmart, at 140.91 USD and down 2.59% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), is the volume-risk test.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The warning sign is that price rises have reached the cheapest products: even Japan's favourite snack has its first-ever price hike [[n1418]]. When that happens, volume elasticity is next to be tested, and Nestlé at 119.00 CHF, -8.11% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), shows investors already discount it.
Narrative

Healthcare is defensive but not cheap enough to lead. XLV closed at 131.58 USD, +2.63% over five sessions and -5.64% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), with the XBI biotech ETF down 17.76% over 20 sessions as higher yields weigh on long-duration biotech.
Reported

The U.S. granted full approval to Moderna's COVID vaccine in adults [[n0729]], and Moderna rose 13.24% over five sessions to 172.74 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Pfizer stopped development of a once-promising heart drug, handing rights back to Ionis [[n0697]], while J&J's fourth quarter was boosted by prescription drugs and medical devices [[n1011]].
EPS Upside Watch

AbbVie's new migraine drugs could each pull in $2B at peak, one analyst says [[n0642]]. Merck, up 6.57% over 20 sessions at 81.92 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), still has to overcome Reuters' finding that its COVID pill is the last choice for U.S. patients [[n0683]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Eli Lilly's warning that the FDA could deny expanded use of its arthritis drug for eczema [[n0487]] is a reminder that regulatory risk, not rates, drives single-name dispersion in this sector; Lilly is down 8.63% over 20 sessions at 248.28 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).
Narrative

Materials are the inflation hedge with real earnings behind it. XLB rose 1.54% to 85.75 USD, and fertiliser led: CF Industries jumped 8.12% to 74.46 USD and Mosaic 9.11% to 43.59 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).
Reported

U.S. Steel set a new stock buyback after the metal-price surge [[n0545]], and Freeport-McMoRan's CEO says copper demand will continue to boom [[n0350]]; Freeport rose 4.84% to 39.02 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).
EPS Upside Watch

Nutrien is eyeing a potash production boost amid turmoil in Russia and Belarus [[n0657]], a direct volume upgrade for North American producers. Aluminum at 3,077.50 USD/t, up 11.81% over 20 sessions, supports Alcoa at 58.17 USD, and palladium at 2,343.20 USD/oz, up 28.61% over 20 sessions, keeps autocatalyst costs high for carmakers (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).
⚡ Breaking Convention

AgWeb reports grain markets rattled by the threat of war between Russia and Ukraine, driving wheat prices higher [[n1831]]. The fertiliser bid is therefore partly a geopolitical premium, and it would fade faster than the metals bid if diplomacy holds.
Narrative

Real estate is the most rate-exposed sector. XLRE fell 0.68% to 47.02 USD and is down 8.40% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), as a 10-year yield of 1.81%, up 18 bps over 20 observations, lifts the discount rate on long-duration rents (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-01).
Reported

Forbes says Blackstone might reach its $1 trillion goal four years ahead of schedule [[n0608]], evidence that private real-estate demand is intact, and the Joint Center for Housing Studies describes a record-breaking rental market [[n1994]].
EPS Upside Watch

Rents are the upside: Prologis is eyeing a massive South Bronx printing-plant site [[n0835]], a signal that urban logistics demand stays tight enough to fund higher land costs. Rates are already hitting housing-linked names: Barron's says Toll was double downgraded on rising rates [[n0375]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Fortune says forecast models put the peak rate of home-price growth behind us [[n1962]], and Bloomberg warns that mortgage-bond weakness threatens the U.S. corporate debt market [[n2034]]. Spread widening, not occupancy, is the listed REIT risk, which is why private-market strength is not translating into public prices.
Narrative

Utilities lost their defensive bid on the rebound: XLU fell 1.33% to 68.33 USD, with Southern Company down 2.16% and Duke Energy 1.53% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Rising yields hurt bond proxies most.
Reported

Georgia Power plans to double renewables and ditch all coal [[n0802]], a capex story that needs cheap capital, while PG&E customers are seeing bills rise because of higher natural gas prices [[n1811]] and Duke Energy Florida customers face minimum $30 bills [[n0486]]: affordability, not demand, is the regulatory risk.
EPS Upside Watch

NextEra at 77.23 USD, down 15.74% over 20 sessions, already prices a lot of rate risk; POWER Magazine's spotlight on a new era for NextEra [[n0825]] frames the growth case, but the multiple needs lower yields to expand. Merchant generators such as Vistra, at 21.65 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), are the exception that can benefit from higher power prices.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The energy-security optionality sits upstream of regulated utilities: Bloomberg notes volatility raging in uranium stocks as clean tech takes a beating [[n0862]], yet Cameco rose 4.17% to 20.24 USD while the utility index fell (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).
Narrative

European autos are rebounding. The SXAP tracker ETF (EXV5.DE) rose 1.45% to 61.73 EUR and is up 3.00% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), and Daimler officially became Mercedes-Benz Group as the carmaker chases a higher valuation [[n0771]].
Reported

CNBC reports Toyota remains the world's biggest car seller and widened its lead on Volkswagen [[n0543]]. ACEA data show commercial vehicle registrations rose 9.6% in 2021 but fell 8.4% in December [[n1711]], more consistent with supply constraints than with collapsing demand.
EPS Upside Watch

GM's expectation that production returns to normal this year as the chip shortage eases [[n1117]] is the read-across: Mercedes-Benz Group at 70.16 EUR and BMW at 94.29 EUR carry operating leverage to volumes, and Renault is up 8.75% over 20 sessions at 35.11 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).
⚡ Breaking Convention

China is the hidden risk. The South China Morning Post reports sales surging at Xpeng, Li Auto and NIO [[n0838]], and Reuters says GAC scolded Stellantis over its joint-venture plan [[n0347]], so Europe's premium brands face share and partner risk in their most profitable market.
Narrative

Semiconductors are rebounding inside a downtrend: SOXX closed at 483.46 USD, +5.05% over five sessions and -12.59% over 20, with ASML at 681.48 USD and the TSMC ADR at 123.05 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).
Reported

SK Hynix sees supply-chain issues improving in the second half and more chip demand [[n0418]], and Samsung published its fourth-quarter and full-year results [[n1054]], closing at 73,300.00 KRW (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-28). Equipment is the soft spot: MarketWatch says Lam Research noted fresh supply-chain issues that cast a pall over the group [[n0382]].
EPS Upside Watch

STMicro's plan to double investments to meet high chip demand [[n0419]] supports equipment orders, and Lam at 589.47 USD, down 18.75% over 20 sessions, has the most room to rerate if supply issues clear. Nvidia's 10.37% five-session bounce to 246.38 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01) shows how quickly leaders recover once forced selling is exhausted.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Industrial policy is becoming the binding constraint: GlobalWafers' Siltronic deal failed as Germany missed the deadline [[n1225]], a reminder that wafer and tool supply chains are now negotiated by governments.

earnings_pattern.title: Guidance beats the beat: forward visibility is the only currency
parts: Rewarded

Investors are paying for forward visibility. Alphabet beat earnings expectations, Al Jazeera reported [[n0807]], and Reuters says Google propelled record revenue and drove the shares up 8% [[n0095]]. UPS hit a record high on a brighter view [[n0858]], GM rose 2.54% after forecasting earnings at or near record levels as the chip shortage eases [[n0800]], and CNBC reports Exxon's shares rose as profit topped estimates [[n0787]]; XOM closed +6.41% at 80.83 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). The common thread is not the size of the beat but a credible path for 2022.
Punished

Weak or cut guidance is punished regardless of the quarter just reported. PayPal plunged on weak earnings guidance [[n0831]], and Barron's says Teradyne's earnings were great but the stock was crushed on guidance [[n0426]]. AT&T sank after saying it will slash its annual dividend 47% following the WarnerMedia spinoff [[n0747]], closing -4.24% at 24.42 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). In Europe, Bloomberg reports Saipem investors questioning the CEO's strategy after a surprise profit warning [[n1129]], and Reuters says Imperial Oil missed profit estimates as cold weather hit output [[n1123]]. Reuters also reports Casino's shares slumping after a profit warning [[n1095]].
Pattern

Three filters explain the dispersion. First, forward guidance outweighs trailing beats. Second, pricing power is rewarded over volume: Starbucks will raise prices again, citing higher costs for supplies and workers [[n1131]]. Third, payout cuts are punished outright, however strategic the rationale, as AT&T's reaction shows. Costs are the common enemy, with Bloomberg reporting McDonald's profit took a hit from labor and commodity costs [[n0387]].
Attention into EPS

Attention now moves to Meta Platforms (FB), where analysts estimate metaverse efforts already generate close to $3 billion a year in revenue [[n1037]], and to Amazon, where GeekWire's preview has analysts expecting record revenue but lower profits [[n0752]]. Further out, S&P Global has scheduled its fourth-quarter results for Tuesday, February 8 [[n1053]]. After Alphabet, the bar for ad platforms is higher, and investors will test whether Google's strength is industry-wide or company-specific.
Playbook

Buy post-earnings strength only where results or guidance reset the outlook higher (Alphabet's record quarter, AMD's 2022 outlook), fade guidance cuts (PayPal) and avoid dividend-cut stories (AT&T). Trigger: the after-hours gains holding through the first full session. What changes the call: a Meta print that disappoints on outlook would show the ad strength is Google-specific and would cap the whole mega-cap rebound.

underowned.title: Fertiliser producers: the Russia–Belarus supply premium
parts: Attention Gap

Fertiliser sits far from the earnings-season spotlight, yet CF Industries jumped 8.12%, Mosaic 9.11% and Nutrien 4.74% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Farm Policy News reports Russia–Ukraine tensions unnerving grain markets [[n1385]], and CME Group notes farming input costs are rising [[n1714]].
Exposure & Risk

Exposure runs through CF, MOS and NTR, with soybeans at 1,528.50 US cents/bu, up 13.73% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), supporting farm incomes and fertiliser affordability. The risk is a diplomatic de-escalation that removes the supply premium quickly.
Trigger to Watch

Successful Farming quotes an analyst saying grain exports are likely to be disrupted in a Russia–Ukraine conflict [[n1800]]; any sanction touching Belarusian potash would be the trigger for a second leg.

underowned.title: Japanese chip-equipment: priced for a downturn customers do not see
parts: Attention Gap

Tokyo Electron is down 16.46% over 20 sessions at 55,370.00 JPY and Advantest 10.55% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), even as Reuters reports the U.S. Commerce Department saying the chip shortage will persist [[n1727]] and Axios warns the next microchip crisis will be bigger [[n1818]].
Exposure & Risk

Data Center Dynamics adds that U.S. firms hold just five days' worth of semiconductor supplies [[n1729]]. Exposure: Tokyo Electron and Advantest, with SK Hynix's results [[n0526]] and its last close of 120,500.00 KRW, +6.17% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-28), as customer-side confirmation. Risk: Teradyne's guidance-led selloff shows test-equipment orders can roll over without warning.
Trigger to Watch
SOXX regaining its 553.10 USD close of January 3 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-03) would confirm that equipment names are being re-rated with the chip group rather than left behind.

underowned.title: Uranium and nuclear fuel: energy security the market is not paying for
parts: Attention Gap

Bloomberg says volatility is raging in uranium stocks as clean tech takes a beating [[n0862]], and MoneyWeek is explaining how to invest in uranium as nuclear power returns [[n1833]]. URA is down 12.16% over 20 sessions at 21.23 USD, while Cameco rose 4.17% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).
Exposure & Risk

Exposure: Cameco, URA and Centrus Energy, which closed at 43.26 USD, down 17.93% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Risk: the group trades with clean-tech beta, so a rate-led growth selloff hits it first, even though Nature finds nuclear power and renewables are both associated with national decarbonization [[n1750]].
Trigger to Watch
Forum Energy Metals buying former Cameco deposits [[n0797]] shows asset demand; a policy move that treats nuclear as part of Europe's gas-security answer would be the catalyst.

underowned.title: European banks: rate leverage with a sanctions caveat
parts: Attention Gap

HSBC is up 15.27% over 20 sessions at 543.50 GBp and Societe Generale 4.40% at 33.33 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), yet attention stays on U.S. tech. Deutsche Bank reported 2021 profit before tax of € 3.4 billion [[n1035]], and UniCredit's Andrea Orcel says it will not deviate from its capital returns strategy [[n0463]].
Exposure & Risk

Exposure: HSBC, Societe Generale and Raiffeisen Bank International, which is up 5.59% over five sessions at 25.32 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Risk: The New York Times warns U.S. sanctions aimed at Russia could take a wide toll [[n1338]], and lenders with eastern exposure are first in line.
Trigger to Watch
Reuters' account of how the Bank of England plans to reverse QE [[n1224]] is the template; any ECB signal on rates or balance sheet would be the trigger.

crypto.title: Crypto: a beta bounce while the plumbing gets built
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin ended its last completed UTC day at 38,743.27 USD, +0.68% on the day and +4.32% over five sessions but -11.85% over 20; Ether rose 3.86% to 2,792.12 USD and Solana 10.27% to 109.98 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-01). The bounce tracks the Nasdaq rebound rather than a crypto-specific catalyst, and USA Today's experts blamed the January drawdown on uncertainty in traditional markets and Fed concerns [[n0911]]. Equity proxies are still lagging over 20 sessions: Coinbase is down 21.24% at 197.73 USD, MicroStrategy 33.19% at 373.00 USD and GBTC 23.34% at 23.73 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), a sign that leverage, not conviction, is still being unwound. BITO, the futures-based ETF, closed at 24.20 USD and is down 16.41% over 20 sessions.
New / Most Important

Private capital keeps flowing into infrastructure: FTX raised $400 million at a $32 billion valuation [[n0938]], though Bloomberg says struggling IPOs give its CEO pause on going public [[n0961]], and Solana wallet Phantom raised $109M [[n0946]]. Regulation is tightening in parallel. India will tax cryptocurrencies at 30% [[n0956]], Russia values local crypto at $200 billion as rules near [[n0960]], and the IMF urged El Salvador to remove Bitcoin as legal tender [[n0884]]. Security remains the tail risk after hackers seized $80 million from Qubit [[n0916]]. Governance links to mainstream finance are deepening too: Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke is joining the board of Coinbase [[n0945]].
Playbook

Action: treat Bitcoin as a high-beta Nasdaq proxy and add Ether or Solana only on confirmed strength. Trigger: Bitcoin reclaiming its 43,949.10 USD close of January 12 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-01-12) would signal that the drawdown is over rather than paused. What changes the call: a renewed Nasdaq selloff, or a regulatory shock from a major jurisdiction; Paul Krugman's warning of disturbing parallels with the subprime meltdown [[n0919]] captures the bear case. Size crypto as a satellite to the equity book, not as a hedge against it.

flows.title: Liquidity: central banks drain, credit frays at the edges, buybacks fill the gap
parts: Global Liquidity

The liquidity regime is turning from abundant to scarce. Reuters explains that the Fed is planning to cut its balance sheet [[n1239]], after the central bank flagged a hike 'soon' and significant balance-sheet reduction [[n1245]]. The Bank of England is further along, with ING publishing a guide to its quantitative tightening [[n1212]], although The Economist argues QT is no substitute for higher interest rates [[n1258]]. The St. Louis Fed is studying how asset purchases reshaped bank balance sheets [[n1269]], which is exactly the reserve base that balance-sheet reduction will now drain. China is the counterweight, with Bloomberg describing a central bank seizing the moment for stimulus as the Fed hikes [[n0120]]. The net effect for global portfolios is that dollar liquidity tightens while Chinese policy loosens, a combination that favours selective emerging-market exposure over broad risk.
Rates & Dollar

The front end is repricing fastest. The 2-year yield rose 40 bps over 20 observations to 1.18% and the 3-month bill 11 bps to 0.19%, while the 30-year added only 11 bps to 2.12%, leaving 30Y-10Y at +31 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-01). Treasury ETFs show the duration pain, with TLT down 1.79% and IEF 1.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). The dollar has paused: Reuters says it slid as its rally took a breather and may have seen a short-term peak [[n0050]]. DXY closed at 96.39 points, +0.46% over five sessions and +0.16% over 20, so the pause is a consolidation rather than a reversal. Housing finance has not yet absorbed the move either, with MONEY reporting mortgage rates moving lower on February 1 [[n1997]], so the transmission of tighter policy is still ahead.
Credit Check

Credit is fraying at the edges, not breaking. Reuters reports record outflows from U.S. high-yield bond ETFs in January [[n1273]], and HYG is down 2.58% over 20 sessions at 84.73 USD, the same decline as LQD at 127.73 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). That parity matters: investment-grade losses come mostly from duration, high-yield losses from spread. Reuters also notes tech-light corporate bonds have swerved the worst of the stock market woes [[n1232]], while Bloomberg warns that mortgage-bond weakness threatens the U.S. corporate debt market [[n2034]], a further risk for spread-sensitive buyers. EMB, down 2.50% over 20 sessions at 105.28 USD, shows emerging-market dollar debt absorbing the Fed shock, consistent with Al Jazeera's report that looming hikes have emerging markets dreading deja vu [[n2009]].
Equity & Fund Flows

Primary markets are closed to the speculative end: WeTransfer's owner cancelled its IPO citing market volatility [[n1250]], and Global Finance says IPOs delivered their worst returns in a decade [[n1257]]. Companies are filling the gap with buybacks, from Hong Kong's Bank of East Asia proposing a $372 million repurchase [[n1252]] to U.S. Steel's new programme [[n0545]]. Insider and activist buying is the other bid: Netflix co-CEO Reed Hastings bought $20 million of shares after the drop [[n0517]], and Reuters reports Pershing Square taking a new position in Netflix [[n0214]]. Supply is coming from founders and families, with MacKenzie Scott selling $8.5B worth of Amazon stock [[n0685]] and the Mittal family raising €1.6 bn from ArcelorMittal share sales [[n0821]]. Australia's Future Fund, which topped $200b, is backing active managers [[n0060]].
Portfolio Implication

Rotate rather than de-risk: hold quality equities with buyback capacity and raised guidance, keep duration short, prefer investment-grade over high-yield and treat the dollar's pause as a consolidation, not a top. Trigger: HYG falling below its 84.73 USD close while the 2-year keeps rising would mean credit is starting to price the Fed, not just ETF outflows. What changes the call: a growth scare that pulls the 2-year back toward 0.78% would restore duration as the better hedge. Gold, at 1,801.50 USD/oz and +0.08% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), has not rallied with inflation; it is a geopolitical hedge, and the World Gold Council's full-year demand trends [[n1683]] are the check on whether physical buying will support it.

anticipatory.title: Meta Platforms (FB): can Google's ad beat travel?
parts: What Is Priced

Meta Platforms (FB) closed at 319.00 USD, +6.28% over five sessions but -5.77% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), ahead of Alphabet's print, and Deadline's report of YouTube ad sales of $8.6B and Search at $43B [[n0870]] now raises the bar. Whether the gap to Alphabet closes depends on whether the next print shows the same advertiser demand.
Conditional Expression

If the report confirms ad strength and frames metaverse spending clearly, FB can close the gap: express it with long FB against Snap at 33.66 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). If guidance disappoints, Snap and Pinterest at 30.01 USD are the second-order shorts, because the market would read Google's strength as search-specific.
Risk

Strategy credibility is the risk. The WSJ reported Facebook's cryptocurrency venture will wind down and sell assets [[n0247]], and Diem's CEO confirmed the sale of its assets to Silvergate [[n0705]]; a heavier metaverse budget with no revenue path would test investors' patience quickly. Bolt-on deals such as the Accusonus acquisition Reuters says Meta is close to [[n0792]] are cheap by comparison.

anticipatory.title: January payrolls: Omicron noise against a March hike
parts: What Is Priced

The 2-year yield at 1.18%, up 40 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-01), prices a March start that CNBC says the Federal Reserve has pointed to [[n1242]]. With 4.6 million more openings than unemployed workers in December [[n1996]], the labour market looks tight enough that the Fed will treat a weak headline as noise.
Conditional Expression

The White House warns an Omicron spike could skew the January jobs report [[n1983]], while Time reports wage growth notched a record increase [[n1958]]. If payrolls are weak but wages stay strong, the curve flattens further: hold 2s10s flatteners. If payrolls are strong, the front end has upside yield risk and long-duration growth is the short.
Risk

The risk is a misread. A soft headline driven by sick leave could trigger a reflexive duration rally that the Fed then dismisses, so fading a weak print may be right but painful in the first session. Marketplace frames the debate as how many times the Fed will raise rates, not whether [[n2046]], which frames the debate around the pace of hikes rather than whether they start.

anticipatory.title: Russia–Ukraine: diplomacy priced, sanctions not
parts: What Is Priced

Brent at 89.16 USD/bbl, wheat at 769.00 US cents/bu after a 5.99% five-session drop, and TTF down 18.61% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01) say diplomacy is partly priced. The BBC reports powers clashing at the UN Security Council [[n1386]], while PBS says Putin accuses the U.S. of ignoring Russian demands but says talks are still possible [[n1383]].
Conditional Expression

If talks hold, the energy and grain premium fades: sell TTF rallies and buy European cyclicals through FEZ. If they fail, the US Senate is contemplating the 'mother of all sanctions' [[n1392]]: long defence (Lockheed Martin, Rheinmetall at 93.22 EUR, up 8.04% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01)), long wheat and long gas.
Risk

CNBC reports analysts warning that Russia is willing to go to war and incur sanctions over Ukraine [[n1364]]. A sudden military move would gap prices through stops, so the conditional trades need options rather than outright futures. Bloomberg's reporting that an invasion would come at a high price [[n1372]] is the argument for diplomacy, not a guarantee of it.

anticipatory.title: Bank of England: a February hike plus QT
parts: What Is Priced

A Reuters poll expects the Bank of England to raise rates again in February as inflation surges [[n1156]], after UK inflation jumped to its highest in 30 years [[n1149]]. Euronews reports sterling strength against the euro as markets eye the BoE [[n1255]], and the FTSE 100 at 7,535.80 points is up 0.41% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), outperforming the STOXX 600.
Conditional Expression

If the BoE confirms a hike and outlines active gilt sales, the Reuters commentary that a second rise sounds the QT klaxon [[n1178]] becomes the base case: favour UK banks such as HSBC over gilts. If the bank hesitates, the relative trade unwinds.
Risk

The Economist says the BoE is determined to prevent a wage-price spiral [[n1172]], yet the ONS documents the strain energy prices put on households [[n1115]]. Tightening into an energy squeeze risks a policy error that hits UK domestic cyclicals hardest, as companies such as the Irn-Bru maker raise prices on fizzing inflation [[n1229]].

catalysts.title: Alphabet (GOOGL)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Alphabet's fourth-quarter profit rose 36% to $20.64 billion, The Seattle Times reports [[n1108]], and Shacknews confirms a 20-for-1 stock split [[n0805]]. Profit growth at this scale argues the ad cycle is intact, and the split widens the buyer base.
Price Hurdle & Risk

GOOGL closed at 2,752.88 USD (+1.73%), still below its 2,899.83 USD close of January 3 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). Reclaiming that level would confirm the re-rating; the risk is that rising yields cap the multiple even as earnings rise.
Trade Expression

Buy if the after-hours gain holds through the first full session, with a stop below the 2,752.88 USD close (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), and size it as the core of the mega-cap growth sleeve.

catalysts.title: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

CNBC reports AMD rose 10% after hours on a strong 2022 sales outlook [[n0744]]. Guidance of that kind is exactly what the market is rewarding, and it lands on a stock that fell 22.27% over 20 sessions to 116.78 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). The stock had already gained 5.08% over five sessions into the print.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The hurdle is the 150.24 USD close of January 3 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-03); the risk is a broader semiconductor de-rating if supply-chain warnings like Lam's spread, or if the 2-year keeps climbing.
Trade Expression
Buy on a hold of the after-hours gap, add if SOXX holds its +5.05% five-session gain, and stop below 116.78 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01).

catalysts.title: Exxon Mobil (XOM)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Exxon posted its biggest profit in seven years [[n0788]], earned $23 billion in 2021 and initiated a $10 billion share repurchase programme [[n1268]]. MarketWatch adds that it will combine its chemical and refining businesses in a cost-cutting reorganization [[n0789]]. Cash returns plus cost cuts make it the cleanest large-cap way to own the energy premium.
Price Hurdle & Risk

XOM closed at 80.83 USD, +6.41% on the day and +27.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01); the hurdle is holding the post-results gap. The risk is an Iran deal or a diplomatic de-escalation that deflates Brent.
Trade Expression
Hold core positions, add on pullbacks toward the gap, and hedge with Brent puts.

catalysts.title: AT&T (T)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

AT&T opted for a spin-off in the WarnerMedia–Discovery transaction and its shares fell on the dividend hit, Deadline reports [[n0746]]; Media Play News says Wall Street disagrees with the structure [[n0745]]. Income investors lose their reason to own the stock.
Price Hurdle & Risk

T closed at 24.42 USD, -4.24% on the day and -7.78% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). The risk to the bearish view is that the post-spin AT&T screens as a cheap, focused telecom once the payout reset is absorbed.
Trade Expression

Avoid or underweight; revisit only if the stock stabilises above its 25.43 USD close of January 3 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-03). Verizon, at 53.20 USD and up 1.45% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01), is the cleaner telecom income alternative.

catalysts.title: Starbucks (SBUX)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The WSJ says Starbucks' sales rose as cost pressures increased at the coffee chain [[n0842]], and Restaurant Dive reports union organizing has reached 60 stores in 19 states [[n0096]]. The New York Times adds that it will raise prices again, citing higher costs for supplies and workers [[n1131]]. Labour cost and union risk compound each other.
Price Hurdle & Risk

SBUX closed at 98.76 USD, -15.36% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01). The hurdle for bulls is its 116.68 USD close of early January; the risk to the bearish view is that price increases fully offset costs.
Trade Expression
Underweight while cost and union headlines dominate; cover if the next print shows margins expanding despite wage pressure.

catalysts.title: Spotify (SPOT)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Spotify's Joe Rogan controversy dominates: The Week says the stock rebounded after Rogan's apology [[n0714]], and the BBC reports the White House praised Spotify's new Covid disclaimers [[n1839]]. The next print must show the row did not dent subscribers.
Price Hurdle & Risk

SPOT closed at 203.62 USD, +3.75% on the day but -16.60% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-01); Loudwire notes the stock had dropped 25% so far in 2022 [[n0588]]. Vanity Fair quotes Rogan insisting he is not trying to spread misinformation [[n0688]]; the risk is subscriber churn or advertiser flight if the row reignites.
Trade Expression
Stay neutral into the print; buy only if subscriber guidance holds and the stock clears 244.16 USD, its close of January 3 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-03).
